# Selecting and editing
Press 3 for Select mode. M, or [bold]Enable selection tools[/bold] in the Tools tab, also turns it on and off.
## Selecting
- [bold]Click an entity[/bold]: select it. - [bold]Click bare floor[/bold]: select that tile and everything on it. - [bold]Shift+click[/bold]: add or take out an entity or a tile. - [bold]Drag[/bold]: select every tile in the box and everything on them. The drag can start in space; it takes the first grid it reaches. - [bold]Right click[/bold]: drop the drag, then the paste, then the selection. Escape drops the selection.
Selected tiles travel with the selection. Moving, rotating, mirroring, copying and deleting take the floor too.
## Editing
[bold]Drag the selection[/bold] Move it. R while dragging turns it. [bold]R[/bold] Rotate clockwise [bold]F[/bold] Mirror left to right [bold]Shift+F[/bold] Mirror top to bottom [bold]Delete[/bold] Delete it [bold]Ctrl+C[/bold] Copy [bold]Ctrl+X[/bold] Cut [bold]Ctrl+V[/bold] Paste
The Tools tab has the same actions as buttons.
Paste shows a preview on the cursor. R turns it. Click to put it down. Shift+click puts it down and keeps the preview for another copy. Right click drops it. A paste in space lands on the grid it was copied from, or on the nearest grid if that one is gone.
Mirroring flips rotations, pipe fittings and one-sided decals. Lopsided sprites, such as a chair's armrest or a sign's text, keep their look.
## Undo
Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes. It works in every mode and covers placing, erasing, tiles, decals, shapes, pipes, links and the selection tools.
- Each mapper has their own history of 30 steps. The oldest go first. - History is lost when you disconnect. - Adding or removing a z-level can't be undone. - A mob that was erased can't be brought back, and mobs can't be copied.
## Size limits
A selection or an erase covers at most 4096 tiles. One copy, paste, delete or undo step touches at most 2000 entities, contents included. A copy or paste carries at most 4096 decals. Anything over a limit is refused whole.
## Whole grids
Every grid on the Grids tab has a [bold]Delete[/bold] button, and [bold]Delete the grid under me[/bold] picks the grid you are over. Either one takes you to the grid and shows its tiles and entities in red, then asks you to confirm. Undo brings it back. Grids over 256 by 256 tiles have to be selected and deleted in parts.
[bold]Hide walls[/bold] in the Tools tab hides every wall for you, so you can see and click what's behind them.
